title: All About Ransomware

reader_summary.headline: Hi, and welcome to the A16Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, and welcome to the A16Z podcast. Today's episode is all about ransomware. We've covered a lot of different types of organized cybercrime and hacks on our show over the years. But in just the last couple years, ransomware in particular has grown into a multi-billion dollar industry.

key_points.text: We've covered a lot of different types of organized cybercrime and hacks on our show over the years.
key_points.evidence_quote: We've covered a lot of different types of organized cybercrime and hacks on our show over the years, many of which you can find at A16Z.com slash hacked.

key_points.text: It's evolved from taking systems and servers hostage to stealing data, and it's capable of shutting down global organizations.
key_points.evidence_quote: It's evolved from taking systems and servers hostage to stealing data, and it's capable of shutting down global organizations.

key_points.text: In recent months, ransomware groups directly shut down Kia Motors' North American IT systems.
key_points.evidence_quote: In recent months, ransomware groups directly shut down Kia Motors' North American IT systems, indirectly led to the death of a patient due to hospital ransomware, and allegedly stole sensitive files from a law firm whose clients include former President Trump.

key_points.text: So in this quick explainer episode, Tom Hoffman, the SVP of Intelligence at Flashpoint Intel.
key_points.evidence_quote: So in this quick explainer episode, Tom Hoffman, the SVP of Intelligence at Flashpoint Intel, which monitors ransomware criminal syndicates and assists organizations with prevention and response, shares his expertise with us.

thesis: The episode explains that ransomware has evolved from taking systems hostage to stealing data and is now a multi-billion dollar industry capable of shutting down global organizations. Tom Hoffman describes ransomware as a business model rather than a technical threat, noting that criminal groups repurpose existing infrastructure to monetize attacks by encrypting systems and leveraging victim insurance policies.
